watchOut: The same page says a turboprop charter "starts at around $2,000 an hour" and a heavy jet is "closer to $10,000 an hour". Its table shows $4,000 to $4,900 and $15,077 to $16,664.
It states the segment fee as $4.50 per passenger. The FAA lists $5.30 for 2026.
feesNamed: Landing fees ($100 to $1,500 per flight, as stated)
Fuel surcharge (starts around $300 an hour when applicable)
name: Stratos Jets
roleBasis: Its homepage calls it an "ARGUS-Certified Broker" and describes "brokering on-demand charter flights".
summary: Charter broker with a seven-row hourly table and an itemized fee list, at the high end of the published ranges.
differentiator: Among the highest hourly ranges we read from any provider, and the page does not say whether they are base or all-in, which changes how to read the gap with the lower tables. It lists fee ranges for landing, handling, fuel and segment fees.
priceNote: The page says a membership lets you lock an hourly rate across five aircraft categories and pay as you fly.
operatorDisclosure: Says it runs an ARGUS CHEQ report on the aircraft before presenting a quote. The pages we read do not say whether the operator is named.
bestFor: Buyers who want fee ranges laid out and are comparing a membership against on-demand.
skipIf: You are using its table as a base rate to compare against other base-rate tables. The basis is not stated.
